8	## Goal
9	
10	Every switching mode should showcase its mechanism on the SAME
11	RVV-intrinsic GEMM, so the suite reads as "one workload, the 4 switching
12	modes": CSR, PC, icount, and SimPoint (whose profile / per-phase drain /
13	archive stages live inside `./hsim run --mode simpoint`).
14	
15	We reuse the existing GEMM `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c` (16x16x16 outer-product,
16	`__riscv_vle32` / `__riscv_vmacc_vx` / `__riscv_vse32`).
17	
18	## Why two builds of one source
19	
20	`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:471-485`: in icount/slice/bbv modes the default CSR
21	matcher is STILL registered. A workload containing `csrwi 0x7C0,0` drains AT the
22	marker and `exit(200)`s before any count target inside the kernel is reached. So:
23	
24	- Marker-driven demos (csr, pc, archive, simpoint) need the markers -> MARKED build.
25	- Coun/profile demos (icount, bbv, slice) need a marker-free workload -> MARKERLESS.
26	
27	Per user decision: one source, a preprocessor macro toggles the markers, built twice.
28	
29	### Confirmed findings (probed on the built artifacts)
30	- `nm -n rt_c_v_matmul.elf` -> only `main`, `_hybrid_enter_pc`, `_hybrid_exit_pc`.
31	  The kernel is inlined at `-O1`, so a PC-range assertion has no symbol to anchor on.
32	  Fix: mark `vmatmul_kernel` `noinline` (also keeps it in the ROI per
33	  `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h:49-51`).

35	  the plugin only `outfile=...`; `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py:237` sets replay
36	  `trigger_kind="csr"`. So T6 and T7 must use the MARKED build.

1	# verify_oracle -- QEMU-oracle differential verification (opt-in, default OFF)
2	
3	Problem: with the QEMU2 handback removed, the post-ROI verification code in a
4	workload never runs, and the e2e suite only checks that a cycle figure exists.
5	Nothing proves the vsim leg executed the ROI *correctly*.
6	
7	Solution (PM decision, 2026-06-12): differential check against QEMU as the
8	oracle. The same ELF runs twice:
9	  run A (oracle):  pure QEMU, plugin drains hybrid_state_v1 at the ROI exit
10	                   boundary (new plugin mode).
11	  run B (hybrid):  the normal QEMU1 -> vsim run; vsim already drains
12	                   hybrid_state_v1 at the same boundary.
13	The pre-ROI path is QEMU in both runs, so the ROI inputs are identical; any
14	architectural divergence inside the ROI (RTL bug, resume bug, drain bug) shows
15	up as a field mismatch. Verification is OPT-IN and default OFF everywhere:
16	`--verify` on `andesim run`, `VERIFY=1` on the e2e harness.
17	
18	Compare policy (fixed, derived from what vsim's drain freshly reads --
19	state_drain.hpp drain_with_passthrough):
20	  strict:  pc, gpr[0..31]; fpr[0..31] (when FLAG_FP); vstart/vtype/vl/
21	           vxsat/vxrm/vcsr + vreg[] (when FLAG_V); magic/version/flags/
22	           hart_id/priv/vlenb (identity).
23	  skipped: mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch, medeleg, mideleg,
24	           mip, mie, satp, pmpcfg[], pmpaddr[] -- passthrough on the vsim
25	           side (copied from QEMU1's ENTRY snapshot, never re-read), so a
26	           compare would test entry-vs-exit, not vsim-vs-oracle.
27	  masked:  mcycle, minstret, mcycle/minstret_at_measure_start -- counters
28	           differ between engines by design.
29	
30	Boundary semantics: the oracle arms on the exit boundary's exec callback and
31	drains on a later one (exec callbacks fire pre-execution, so the capture is
32	post-retire state). EMPIRICAL FINDING (first full-suite run, 20/35 failed):
33	vsim's DMI halt is NOT insn-precise -- the core retires a variable 0-3 more
34	insns while haltreq propagates, so vsim's drained pc lands past the trigger
35	and those slack insns' effects are in its record. Fix: the harness reads
36	vsim's drained pc and passes it as the plugin's `drain_pc=`; the oracle
37	drains at the first post-arm hit of that pc, so both sides sample the SAME
38	architectural point (pc then matches by construction; if vsim's pc is never
39	reached -- a real control-flow divergence -- the oracle never drains and the
40	run fails on its exit code). Limitation: the oracle arms on the first
41	exit-boundary hit; like the hybrid run itself it assumes a single-shot ROI.
42	icount-trigger verify is out of scope (off-by-one window semantics differ;
43	revisit if needed).

1	# roi_markers.md - portable ROI markers (Part A) + trigger rename
2	
3	DECIDED (2026-06-11): Part A + rename `csr` -> `marker`. Scope = F1-F3.
4	Part B (file:line / IDE anchors) is DEFERRED - kept at the bottom for later.
5	
6	## Problem
7	
8	The in-binary ROI markers are `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on
9	the Andes core: the exit marker enables ILM at base 0 and kills any
10	standalone run (`--model fast` trap loop). So today one binary cannot
11	carry markers AND run on all engines. Also the trigger name `csr` is
12	wrong: vsim never executes the CSR; it pre-scans code bytes for the
13	encoding and PC-watches (`csr_trigger.hpp`), and the QEMU plugin matches
14	the encoding at translate time. A marker is "a recognizable byte pattern
15	whose address becomes the trigger PC" - so swap the pattern for one that
16	is a NOP everywhere.
17	
18	## Design: RISC-V HINT pair
19	
20	Integer-computational instructions with rd=x0 are architectural NOPs on
21	every conforming RISC-V core (spec HINT space). New encodings:
22	
23	| Kind    | Asm                     | Encoding match                       |
24	|---------|-------------------------|--------------------------------------|
25	| ENTER   | `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`    | insn == 0x5A002013                   |
26	| EXIT    | `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`    | insn == 0x5A102013                   |
27	
28	RUNTIME (`csrw 0x7C0, rs1`, kind read from rs1 at retire) is DROPPED, not
29	ported: nothing in the repo uses it except its own unit tests. F2 deletes
30	the matcher arm, the `HYBRID_HANDOFF_RUNTIME` case + `decode_csrrw_rs1`
31	in handoff_controller.hpp, and the related unit tests. If a
32	conditional-exit need appears later, re-add as `slt x0, rs1, x0`
33	((insn & 0xFFF07FFF) == 0x00002033).
34	
35	Properties:
36	- True NOP on fast, cycle, hybrid AND real silicon. MILMB hazard gone;
37	  one marker ELF runs standalone everywhere. All MILMB warnings in docs
38	  get deleted.
39	- `slti`/`slt` have no compressed form: the plugin `sz==4` gate and the
40	  vsim 16/32-bit scanner invariant hold unchanged.
41	- No collision with allocated standard hints: Zihintntl is
42	  `add x0, x0, x2..x5` (funct3=000, we use 010), Zihintpause is a FENCE
43	  form. F2 verifies the imm choice against the unpriv spec HINT table
44	  and confirms NOP behavior on the vsim RTL (the real authority).
45

1	# V-scratch reservation: move the transport page out of the program's RAM
2	
3	## Problem (L26)
4	
5	The V-register transport stages 32 vector registers through a 4 KB guest-RAM
6	window at the **compile-time constant** `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MB).
7	That address sits *inside* the program's usable RAM, so a program that places
8	data there (large heap, custom linker script, direct addressing) is silently
9	corrupted on every resume -- even if it never uses V. Demonstrated by
10	`tests/fixtures/break_vscratch.S`.
11	
12	## Core architecture (the fix: scheme D)
13	
14	Put the scratch page **just above the program's declared RAM**, by making the
15	physical mmap one page larger than `--mem-size`. The program is told it has
16	`mem_size`; the simulator quietly maps `mem_size + 4 KB` and parks the scratch
17	in the extra page. No program layout can reach a page above its own ceiling
18	without a bug, so the collision class is removed at the root rather than
19	detected after the fact.
20	
21	```
22	            +----------------+ ram_base + mmap_size            (physical top)
23	V scratch ->|  V scratch 4KB |   mmap_size = mem_size + 4 KB
24	            +----------------+ ram_base + mem_size             (program ceiling)
25	            |  program RAM   |   text / data / heap / stack -- all strictly below
26	            +----------------+ ram_base
27	```
28	
29	Scratch GPA = `ram_base + mmap_size - kVScratchBytes` = the **top page of the
30	mmap**. Both legs already receive `mmap_size`, so the address stays a derived
31	value with **no new field to keep in sync** -- the only change vs the naive
32	"top of RAM" is that the mmap is one page bigger than the program's RAM, which
33	lifts the scratch above everything the program can legally address.
34	
35	Invariant that must hold at every step: **the host stager and the vsim
36	Program-Buffer sweep must use the SAME scratch address.** That is why the
37	"runtime GPA" work (F1) lands as one atomic unit across all three users.
38	
39	## Features

9	## 1. Context
10	
11	`vsim` runs at 5-9 KHz on Andes RISC-V cores. A typical workload spends >99% of cycles in boot, libc init, and warm-up before reaching the kernel under study. Today the only escape hatch is `--save`/`--continue`, which still requires an initial RTL run to reach the snapshot point. There is also already a `--kanata-loop-{start,end,skip,record}` mechanism (`src/main.cpp:183-214`) that identifies the interesting loop iterations.
12	
13	We want: run everything before the ROI in QEMU (functional, MHz), hand the architectural state to Verilator at the ROI boundary, run the ROI cycle-accurately to record kanata/clarity pipeline data, and optionally hand back to QEMU to finish.
14	
15	The intended outcome: 100x-1000x reduction in wall-clock time for benchmarking workflows that only care about steady-state pipeline behavior of a small kernel, with byte-identical kanata output for the recorded window vs. a fully-RTL baseline.

20	
21	### 2.1 The state-exchange problem, reframed
22	
23	A naive hybrid sim has to "transfer" CPU state between two simulators. In practice the state splits into three categories with very different costs:
24	
25	| Category | Items | Size | Strategy |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| Architectural regs | x0..x31, f0..f31, V regs, key CSRs | 4-8 KB | **Copy** via well-defined ABI struct |
28	| Memory | guest RAM, ILM/DLM | MB-GB | **Share** via `mmap` - zero copy |
29	| Microarchitectural state | TLB, caches, BPU, store buffer | KB-MB | **Discard** - let cold starts repopulate |
30	
31	The key trick: **memory does not move**. QEMU runs with `-object memory-backend-file,share=on,mem-path=/dev/shm/vsim-ram`. vsim's `SimpleMemory::data` (`src/platform/simple_memory.hpp:20`) is changed to an `mmap` of the same fd. Both simulators read and write the same physical bytes. The same trick is used by QEMU's CPR (`docs/devel/migration/CPR.rst`) and gem5's `SimpleSwitchableProcessor`. RAM size becomes irrelevant.
32	
33	Microarch state is intentionally discarded. We accept cold caches/BPU on entry into Verilator and rely on the existing `kanata_loop_skip N` mechanism to warm them up before recording. This matches the gem5 "switch + warmup" pattern.
